newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INCE SAYS WILL DECIDE FUTURE AT END OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INCE SAYS WILL DECIDE FUTURE AT END OF SEASON.

text.p: England midfielder Paul Ince said on Thursday he would decide whether to stay with Internazionale Milan at the end of the season, adding he had already rejected an offer from English side Arsenal.
Ince's contract at Inter, where he moved last year from English champions Manchester United, runs to 1999 and he has become a firm favourite with fans at the San Siro stadium.
"Arsenal came looking for me about a month ago but I said 'no'," Ince told reporters at Inter's training ground.
He left open whether his time with Inter would end with the current season, saying he would meet chairman Massimo Moratti then to "clarify my position and see what's best to do".
"I'm not interested in making long term plans now. I'll decide my future in four or five months time," he said.
Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger said on Tuesday he might be interested in buying Ince if Inter put him on the market.

Inter spokesman Sandro Sabatini said earlier on Thursday: "Ince will remain with us for this season and I don't think he will go to Arsenal. We are very satisfied with him... We don't want to put Ince on the market."
Ince has been the subject of racial abuse from opposing fans and has a poor disciplinary record in Italy's serie A.

He was given a four-match ban on Monday for protesting with foul language and abusive gestures after he was sent off during Inter's 1-1 league draw with Reggiana on December 22, his third red card of the season.
Ince said he was surprised by the toughness of the suspension but not by the sending off.

"Stop writing that I have problems with Italian referees. The sending off against Reggiana was right and any English referee would have taken the same decision. Four matches is a bit excessive though and frankly I expected less," he said.
Ince also denied Italian media reports his family was unhappy in Italy and wanted to return to England.
"It's not true at all. Claire, Thomas and I are perfectly happy in Italy," he said.
